svg.title: A native saved-state receipt survives the Python completion window
svg.desc: For one bound tissue-detection entry, the existing save writes tissue section objects to data.qpdata. The shared native publisher hashes those exact bytes and embeds saved_project_state in the same stage result. Its five fields bind the entry, prepared descriptor, process launch, request envelope and saved-state SHA-256. The result also references the tissue generation manifest by its existing path and SHA-256. After the original native child exits normally with status zero and its drain is retained, Python can continue or, if its former owner has exited before mutation evidence or terminal commit, reacquire project control for the exact pending operation. The original child is already complete. Ordinary project inspection supplies the current saved-state checksum; original operation identities and current bytes must match the receipt. The usual stage codec and commit then record the tissue generation and its result status. Geometry, byte marks, identity symbols and time spacing are schematic, not observed values.
